description:
Our revised proposal for the extension and renovation of the property has been meticulously redesigned to align with Hackney’s local planning guidelines and the specific character of the Brownswood Conservation Area. Recognising the concerns raised by the previous rejection regarding the incongruous form and excessive massing of the first-floor level, we have modified the design by increasing the height of the side extension to more closely match the prevailing building heights observed on Queen Drive and Wilberforce Road. This adjustment ensures that the extension is in proportion to the scale of the surrounding properties and eliminates the stepped design, enhancing the visual continuity along the terrace.

Despite being an end-of-terrace property, the proposed extension is set back from the main view when approaching down Digby Crescent. This positioning minimises visual impact and aligns with the architectural precedents seen in the conservation area, thus supporting a more harmonious street scene.

In addition to the architectural and design modifications, the revised proposal includes the creation of an ensuite on the first floor, specifically designed to accommodate elderly grandparents who will be residing in the property. This adjustment follows the request and condition to remove the external steps leading into the basement from our previous application, enhancing the accessibility and safety of the home for less mobile residents. This change not only demonstrates our commitment to creating a more inclusive living environment but also provides a direct benefit to the community by supporting multi-generational living and allowing elderly residents to live comfortably with family. Such considerations align with broader societal objectives of accommodating ageing populations within their existing communities, thus reducing the demand on external care facilities and reinforcing family bonds.

We believe these changes address the previous objections under policies D3 and HC1 of the London Plan 2021, as well as LP1, LP3, and LP17 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033. The refined design not only respects but enhances the character and appearance of the area, adhering to the guidelines set forth in the Hackney Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD 2009. Our proposal incorporates sustainable building practices and materials to improve energy efficiency, aligning with environmental targets and contributing positively to the community. Through thoughtful design and engagement with local planning policies, this project aims to provide substantial improvements to the functionality and aesthetic appeal of the property, ensuring it complements and enhances the local heritage and community fabric.
